summary: Small top-up order: Maggi 3 cartons and Parle-G 1 carton. Mom's Magic is a slow mover. The 2 cartons from last time are unsold because of price, so she asked us not to send more. She rejected the 10+1 scheme as too big for her shop, and reported that Britannia is offering 15-day credit and a display rack. Arjun did not counter either point.
score_reason: An order was taken and the scheme was mentioned. However, the order was small, the scheme was not adapted to the outlet, and Britannia's credit and rack offer went unanswered. Visibility and collections were not covered.

coaching.tip: You asked about last visit's Mom's Magic cartons. That surfaced a slow mover and the price feedback behind it. Keep checking previous stock before booking repeats.

When Mrs. Gupta mentioned Britannia's 15-day credit and rack, don't just move on to closing the order. Acknowledge it, ask how many days of credit she needs, and promise to check with your manager what visibility support Northwind can offer.

When a small shop says the 10+1 scheme is too big, offer a mixed-SKU way to reach ten cartons (Maggi + Parle-G + Tata Tea), or check for a smaller-slab scheme. Also check shelf display and pending dues before you leave.

debrief: Arjun, Gupta Kirana ka visit theek-thaak raha. Maggi teen carton aur Parle-G ek carton ka order mila. Achha kiya ki aapne Mom's Magic ka pichhla stock poocha, isse pata chala do carton abhi tak pade hain. Agli baar jab Britannia ke pandrah din ke udhaar aur rack ki baat aaye, toh wahin ruk ke jawab do aur chhoti dukaan ke liye mixed-carton scheme suggest karo. Next step: agle mangalvar, satrah November ko wapas jaana.
